_meta.description: Full mechanical specification for Mutants & Masterminds 4e equipment, vehicles, and installations, for implementing acquisition, cost, and combat automation. All prose fields are original paraphrases of the functional rules (costs, ranks, DCs, formulas) written for this project — not copied rulebook text. Read mm-equipment-design.md first for the pattern definitions referenced in 'patterns' below. Companion to equipment.json (short always-visible label copy).

currency.name: Equipment Point
currency.note: Equipment is a bundle of power effects carried at the top tier of the Removable flaw. Rather than applying that flaw item by item, the Equipment advantage hands out 5 Equipment Points per rank and items are priced at their undiscounted effect cost. The flaw's limitations still apply in play even though its discount is not recomputed.
currency.reconfigure: At the start of each adventure, or between scenes with access to a headquarters or cache.
currency.notAPower: Equipment does not count as a power. A character built purely from equipment can still be described as having no powers.

categoryKey.utility: A small gadget, mostly built from the Feature effect or a low-rank utility effect
categoryKey.close_weapon: A hand-held weapon used in close combat
categoryKey.ranged_weapon: A projectile, thrown, or energy weapon
categoryKey.accessory: An add-on fitted to another weapon rather than used on its own
categoryKey.grenade: A thrown area attack, consumed on use
categoryKey.explosive: A placed area attack, consumed on use
categoryKey.armor: Worn protection, normally a Protection effect
categoryKey.shield: A carried defence granting Enhanced Defense; requires active use
categoryKey.kit: A bundle or array of other items, priced as a build rather than a fixed line
categoryKey.vehicle: A built platform with its own Size/Strength/Toughness/Defense/Speed trait costs
categoryKey.installation: A built fixed structure with its own Size/Toughness/Feature trait costs

patternKey.passive_trait_item: Worn or held; contributes a standing bonus to a trait while possessed. Subject to the equipment no-stacking rule.
patternKey.attack_item: Exposes a usable attack action rather than a standing bonus.
patternKey.skill_aid: Grants a bonus to, or removes a penalty from, a named skill or skill use.
patternKey.conditional_bonus_item: Like passive_trait_item but gated on a declared circumstance or descriptor.
patternKey.sense_item: Grants an Enhanced Senses quality while worn or held.
patternKey.movement_item: Grants a movement effect or mode while worn or held.
patternKey.utility_effect_item: Produces a discrete non-attack effect on use (illumination, restraint, tracking).
patternKey.consumable: Has a limited number of uses that deplete and must be replaced or recharged.
patternKey.container_array: A bundle of other items, priced as an array (costliest in full plus 1 point per alternate) or as a flat list.
patternKey.accessory: Modifies another item rather than standing alone; cost is added to the host item.
patternKey.platform: A vehicle or installation: a sub-build with its own trait-cost table and point pool.
patternKey.feature_slot: A 1-point named Feature on a platform; some are repeatable with escalating effect.
patternKey.gm_adjudicated: The trigger is mechanical but the outcome is a Game Master ruling, not something the engine resolves.

costKindKey.fixed: A flat Equipment Point cost given in the rules
costKindKey.ranked: Cost scales with a small number of defined ranks (see costNote)
costKindKey.per_rank: 1 Equipment Point per rank, rank chosen by the player
costKindKey.built: No fixed cost: assembled from components or trait tables (see implementation)

stackingRule.rule: Equipment bonuses do not stack with each other or with bonuses from other sources — only the single highest applicable bonus applies.
stackingRule.engineNote: Compute equipment contributions as max(), not sum(), per target stat, and then take max() again against non-equipment sources. This is why a character with high native Protection gains nothing from armour.

strengthBasedDamage.baseRule: A Strength-Based Damage effect adds the wielder's Strength rank to the weapon's Damage rank.
strengthBasedDamage.costPerRankDivisor: When modifiers push the effect above 1 point per rank, divide the wielder's Strength rank by the effect's cost per rank and round down; that reduced number is the Strength bonus actually added.
strengthBasedDamage.example: A compound bow with Ranged Strength-Based Damage costs 2 points per rank, so a Strength 5 wielder adds floor(5 / 2) = +2 to the bow's Damage rank.
doesNotApply: Effects costing less than 1 point per rank — Strength is not multiplied for these.
Flat modifiers that do not change cost per rank — the full Strength rank still applies.
strengthBasedDamage.breakageCap: An ordinary weapon can only carry Strength up to its own Toughness (roughly 4 for wood, 7-8 for metal). Exerting more Strength than that breaks the weapon when it is used.
strengthBasedDamage.engineNote: This divisor is separate from the cost engine's effective-rank rule. Cost still prices per-rank Extras against the full effective rank (purchased + Strength); this divisor only limits how much Strength reaches the Damage rank in the first place. Apply the divisor first, then feed the resulting effective rank into both the DC calculation and the Extra pricing.
strengthBasedDamage.materialToughnessNote: Toughness by the material an item's 'implementation.material' names, derived from the printed breakageCap guidance. An item naming no material, or one this table does not list, is never warned about.

equipmentLimits.availability: The GM may restrict ownership of some items (permits, licences, bulk) or charge extra Feature ranks for restricted gear.
equipmentLimits.materialCost: Items have a real-world cost and supply; the GM may block acquisition or replacement in play.
equipmentLimits.damageAndLoss: Equipment is more exposed to damage, malfunction, theft, and loss than a Removable device.
equipmentLimits.extraEffort: Extra Effort used with equipment strains the equipment, not the character: Impaired, then Disabled, then Debilitated. Maintenance or repair clears these, not rest.
equipmentLimits.technologicalLimits: Equipment covers only technology commonly available in the setting — normally real-world tech, not battlesuits, force fields, or shrink rays.

damagingEquipment.rule: Damaged equipment loses 1 Feature or takes a cumulative -1 circumstance penalty on checks involving it per degree of damage.
damagingEquipment.repair: A technical skill check clears the penalty; jury-rigging restores it temporarily.
damagingEquipment.replacement: Time- and resource-dependent, at the GM's discretion. A Hero Point spent on Well-Equipped can produce a replacement as an on-hand item.

onHandEquipment.rule: Spend a Hero Point to have one item on hand, so long as it falls within your Equipment Point allotment (or is worth 5 EP or less if you lack the Equipment advantage).
onHandEquipment.gmGate: The GM decides whether having that item on hand is plausible in the scene.

alternateEquipment.rule: Items with overlapping function, usable one at a time, can be an array: pay the costliest item in full, then 1 Equipment Point per alternate.
alternateEquipment.note: Since most utility items cost 1-2 EP, arraying them saves little and costs flexibility. Arrays pay off for weapons and for vehicles.

whatYouPayFor.rule: Only adventuring gear costs Equipment Points — items with a direct impact on the character's heroic role.
whatYouPayFor.fallback: When in doubt the GM rules; a player wanting to bring a cost-free background element to bear can be charged a Hero Point instead.

weaponTraits.advantageScope: A weapon-granted advantage is a trait of the weapon, not the character: it applies only while wielding that weapon, in exchange for a reduced cost.
weaponTraits.criticalCost: Widening a weapon's threat range by 1 costs 1 Equipment Point, priced like advantages:improved_critical.
weaponTraits.concealedWeapons: A concealable weapon is normally 1 rank of modifiers:subtle — a DC 20 Perception check to spot it before it is drawn. Stacks with the wielder's own Sleight of Hand attempts.
weaponTraits.pairedWeapons: A wielded pair is modelled as modifiers:split: pay 1 extra point for the second weapon, then divide one Attack action's effect between two targets.
weaponTraits.thrownWeapons: A thrown weapon must be retrieved before reuse; that drawback offsets the benefit, so there is no cost change. Sets of throwing weapons are assumed always available unless flawed or a complication is accepted.

vehicleTraitCosts.size: 1 Equipment Point per size rank above 0
vehicleTraitCosts.strength: 1 Equipment Point per +1 Strength above the size baseline
vehicleTraitCosts.toughness: 1 Equipment Point per +1 Toughness above the size baseline
vehicleTraitCosts.defense: 1 Equipment Point per -1 of the size Defense penalty bought off, down to -0
vehicleTraitCosts.speed: The movement effect's normal Power Point cost, paid in Equipment Points
vehicleTraitCosts.powers: The effect's normal Power Point cost, paid in Equipment Points
vehicleTraitCosts.buildOrder: Choose Size first — it sets the baselines for Strength, Toughness, and Defense.

_meta.vehicleSizeExtension: Beyond size rank 5, each further rank adds +2 Strength, +1 Toughness, and -1 Defense (GM option).

vehicleCombat.defenseRank: A moving vehicle's Defense rank equals its current speed rank plus the Defense modifier for its Size.
vehicleCombat.stationary: A stationary vehicle can be attacked as a routine check at DC 10 plus the vehicle's Defense modifier.
vehicleCombat.defensiveCheck: The pilot may take a standard action for evasive manoeuvres, substituting their Vehicles check result modified by the size Defense modifier for the vehicle's Defense Class that round. If that result is lower than the usual Defense Class, apply +1 to the usual DC instead.
vehicleCombat.targetingOccupants: Use the higher of the occupant's Defense or the vehicle's; the occupant usually also has cover and concealment from outside attacks.
vehicleCombat.combatSkillFocus: Vehicle Weapons is its own focus of Close Combat and Ranged Combat. Attacks use Attack + attack advantage (if any) + vehicle combat skill (if any).

vehicleControl.actionType: non-action, but the operator must be able to take at least free actions
vehicleControl.perRound: One control check per round per vehicle; each additional check called for that round raises the DC by +5.
vehicleControl.onFailure: The vehicle crashes into an obstacle or another vehicle. Air and space vehicles with nothing to hit may stall instead; restarting is a Vehicles check against the same DC as the control check.

vehicleCrash.baseDamageRank: the speed rank of the fastest vehicle involved

modifiers.when: per size rank of difference, applied to the smaller vehicle
two degrees of failure on the control check
three or more degrees of failure on the control check

vehicleCrash.sameDirection: Subtract the lower speed rank from the higher to get the effective speed rank of the crash.

occupants.onSuccess: +5 bonus to resist the crash damage

vehicleDamage.hit: The usual cumulative -1 penalty to Damage resistance checks per condition.
vehicleDamage.dazed_or_stunned: Requires a control check and leaves the vehicle Impaired: a cumulative -1 penalty to checks involving it, or the loss of one Feature or one Equipment Point of capability per -1.
vehicleDamage.staggered: One system stops working — weapons or another effect, propulsion (losing 1 speed rank per round until Immobile), or controls (automatically suffering a failed control check each round).
vehicleDamage.incapacitated: The vehicle no longer functions. Water vehicles sink, air vehicles crash, space vehicles may lose life support and drift.
vehicleDamage.extraEffort: Extra Effort with a vehicle ('redlining') strains the vehicle, not the driver: Impaired, then Disabled, then Immobilized. A Disabled vehicle is also Hindered (-1 speed rank). These persist until maintenance.

vehicleMovementModes.multipleModes: Pay the costliest mode in full; take the others as Alternate Effects at 1 point each.

sharedAndAlternate.sharedVehicle: A team splits a vehicle's Equipment Point cost among its members as they see fit.
sharedAndAlternate.alternateVehicles: Multiple vehicles are Alternate Equipment by default: pay the costliest in full, then 1 Equipment Point per additional vehicle of equal or lesser cost.
sharedAndAlternate.sharedInstallation: A shared installation divides its cost among everyone with access. Characters who leave permanently reclaim their contributed ranks.
sharedAndAlternate.alternateInstallations: Also arrayable, with the exception that a genuinely shared installation is paid for jointly and personal installations are paid for separately in full.

installationTraitCosts.size: 1 Equipment Point per size rank; size rank 5 is the free starting point
installationTraitCosts.toughness: 1 Equipment Point per +2 Toughness; Toughness 6 is the free starting point
installationTraitCosts.effects: The effect's normal Power Point cost, paid in Equipment Points

installationTraits.note: The same table as installationTraitCosts, in the numbers the engine reads.

installationPowerLevel.playerOwned: Limited by the series Power Level.
installationPowerLevel.npcOwned: Not strictly limited; the GM may cap at the NPC's Power Level as a guideline.
installationPowerLevel.toughnessCap: Up to twice the series Power Level, since installations have no other defences.
installationPowerLevel.imperviousCap: No greater than the Power Level.
installationPowerLevel.featureLimitSuggestion: The GM may cap Features by size — for example no more than 2 per size rank above 3, and 1 per size rank below that.

environments.vehicles: A vehicle is assumed to provide life support for the environments it is built to travel through, at no point cost. Lacking it is a Quirk or a complication.
environments.installations: An installation is assumed to provide Earth-normal atmosphere, pressure, temperature, and gravity regardless of location, at no point cost. Immunity to anything beyond that needs a Feature.

outOfScope.constructs: Robots, androids, golems, and undead are characters (minions), not equipment. They are acquired through advantages:minion, advantages:sidekick, or effects:summon and belong in a separate constructs reference.
outOfScope.mounts: Treated as vehicles for most guidelines but acquired as Minions, Sidekicks, or Summons; riding uses skills:athletics unless the GM adds a Riding skill.
outOfScope.chaseSequences: Chases and races are check sequences and belong with the challenge rules in mm-actions-adventure.md, not here.

unresolvedReferences.issue: Listed as a weapon advantage in the close-weapon table and in the Wrestling fighting style, but there is no fast_grab entry in the 4e advantage list (advantages.json).
unresolvedReferences.suggestion: Either treat it as a legacy 3e name and map to advantages:agile_grab, or surface it as free text on the item until the rules clarify. Do not silently drop it.

unresolvedReferences.issue: Called a 'weapon advantage' in the Weapon Advantages text and abbreviated to 'Defensive' in the table, but in 4e Defensive Attack is a combat manoeuvre (see mm-actions-adventure.md), not an advantage.
unresolvedReferences.suggestion: Model as an item-granted manoeuvre bonus rather than an advantage reference.

unresolvedReferences.issue: The stock-vehicle weapon descriptions use the legacy effect name 'Blast'.
unresolvedReferences.suggestion: Map to effects:damage with modifiers:ranged. Already normalised in this file's vehicle weapon entries.

printedDiscrepancies.printed: Prose says Reach 3; the close-weapon table prices Reach 2.
printedDiscrepancies.resolution: This file follows the table (Reach 2), since the table drives the cost.

printedDiscrepancies.printed: Prose says Reach 1 or 2; the table prices Reach 2.
Appears in both the close-weapon table (Str-based Damage 1, Improved Critical, Thrown, 3 points) and the thrown-weapon table (Ranged Damage 2, 4 points).
printedDiscrepancies.resolution: Both are kept as separate ids (javelin, javelin_thrown). Let the player pick.

printedDiscrepancies.printed: The Ranged Weapons intro says thrown weapons are Strength-based, but the thrown-weapon table lists plain Ranged Damage with no Strength-Based tag, and shuriken are explicitly excluded.
printedDiscrepancies.resolution: This file follows the table (not Strength-based) and flags the intro text here. Consider making Strength-Based an opt-in checkbox on thrown weapons.

printedDiscrepancies.printed: The Installation Trait Cost table gives Size a starting rank of 0, but the surrounding text and the Structure Size Categories table both put the free starting point at size rank 5.
printedDiscrepancies.resolution: This file uses size rank 5 = 0 points, matching the size table (which is internally consistent: rank 11 = 6 points, rank 1 = -4 points). Treat the trait-cost table's '0' as a typo.

printedDiscrepancies.printed: Listed at Size 2 with a -1 Defense modifier, where Size 2 implies -2.
printedDiscrepancies.resolution: Kept as printed; flag in the UI if a validator recomputes Defense from Size.

printedDiscrepancies.printed: Listed as Toughness 2, below the free baseline of 6, and inconsistent with the 39-point total.
printedDiscrepancies.resolution: Kept as printed with a note; 20 is the arithmetically plausible value.

_meta.vehicleClassesNote: Which movement effect a stock vehicle's printed Speed rank is a rank of, so a plane's Speed reaches the sheet as Flight and a boat's as Swimming. An Exotic vehicle names no default: it carries its own 'movement' block instead.
